proof_summary: For \(n=1093^2-1\), a modular computation gives \(\sum_{j=1}^{1092}(-1)^j/j\equiv0\pmod{1093}\); splitting the defining factorial sum into terms divisible and not divisible by \(1093\) then yields \(1093^{1092}\mid F(n)\), while \(v_{1093}(n!)=1092\). The recurrence for \(F\) and gcd invariance consequently make the two relevant consecutive gcds equal, so the ratio is \(1\), whereas \(n+1=1093^2\) is composite.
